chunks: I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and upon him was a coarse, rough shirt beneath his clothes, and above it a woolen coat, and above it another coarse shirt. I touched it and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The people dislike wearing wool.'

So he said: 'Never! My father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) used to wear it, and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to wear it, and they (peace be upon them) used to wear the roughest of their garments when they stood for salat, and we do that (as well).'

key_terms.أَغْلَظَ ثِيَابِهِمْ: the roughest of their garments — specifically worn during salat as an act of devotion
key_terms.جُبَّةُ صُوفٍ: a woolen coat (jubba) — an outer garment made of wool, associated with ascetic piety
key_terms.قَمِيصٌ غَلِيظٌ خَشِنٌ: a coarse, rough shirt — emphasizing the deliberately austere nature of the garment
key_terms.كَلَّا: Never! — a strong emphatic refutation rejecting the people's dislike of wool
key_terms.لِبَاسُ الصُّوفِ: wearing wool — a practice linked to asceticism and humility in Islamic tradition

ai.seo_question: Did the Shia Imams wear wool or rough clothing during prayer?
ai.summary: A companion of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) sees the Imam wearing multiple layers of coarse woolen garments. When the companion notes that people dislike wearing wool, the Imam firmly rejects this attitude, citing the practice of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) and Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-'Abidin (AS), and revealing that the Imams specifically wore their roughest garments when performing salat. This hadith establishes wearing rough or woolen clothing during prayer as an ascetic practice of the Ahlulbayt, rooted in humility before God and distinct from the general public's preference for softer garments.
